A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LoRA-Mixer work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Reliable comparison is possible despite the conference-format change and extensive appendix reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, routing ablations, cross-domain QA results, and cross-model transfer experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds benchmark, routing-baseline, generalization, hyperparameter, and resource measurements.

M1.justification: Both versions retain serial projection-layer LoRA composition, hard-routing expert training, soft router training, the same RSL and expert-preservation objectives, and top-3 inference. The new surrogate and mirror-descent discussion concerns theoretical analysis; additional training schedules are newly documented implementation details.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluated coverage on BoolQ, HellaSwag, PIQA, QNLI, and MNLI, plus out-of-distribution testing on QQP, RTE, and MRPC. The earlier GLUE adapter-reuse and synthetic cross-domain tasks remain. MBPP appears in the new dataset-statistics table without corresponding results, so its actual evaluation is unclear.

E2.justification: V2 adds PHATGOOSE comparisons in Tables 6 and 21 and controlled routing-loss comparisons against GMoE, DS-MoE, and AESL in Table 8. The existing LoRAHub, MoLE, MixLoRA, LoRA, and LoRA-LEGO comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include a fixed-2K-data routing-loss comparison, PHATGOOSE in-distribution/OOD testing, rank-16 QNLI/MNLI and rank-32 commonsense evaluations, and an alpha/lambda search using a 10% validation split. V2 also introduces resource-measurement protocols and extends router-data budgets to 10K. Newly disclosed settings for retained experiments do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: V2 adds OOD generalization tests, alpha/lambda sensitivity analysis, and parameter, latency, training-time, and memory analyses, while extending the data-size study. V1's numerical individual-expert ablation table is removed, although its discussion survives. Rank, top-K, expert-load, and cross-domain analyses are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Both main texts report averages over three runs, without newly defined confidence intervals, significance tests, or seed reporting. V2 removes v1's checklist statement that experiments were repeated 'more than three times,' eliminating conflicting run-count wording. This is a reporting change, not evidence of a changed run budget.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and the matched rank and cross-domain results remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial benchmark, comparator, hyperparameter, and resource results. In the data-size study, the 4K with/without-RSL means change from 78.51/79.28 to 78.77/79.14; the 3K row disappears and 6K, 8K, and 10K rows appear. V1's individual-expert result table is also removed.

T1.justification: V2 adds explicit smoothing, convexity, and Lipschitz assumptions, mirror-descent convergence statements, and algorithmic-stability generalization bounds in Appendices A.1–A.2. Appendix A.17 replaces v1's auxiliary-loss equilibrium argument with a derivation for a quadratic balancing surrogate. The gradient and routing-variance analysis already existed in v1 Appendix C and is moved into Section 3.3.

C1.justification: V2 shifts contribution emphasis toward RSL: its conclusion presents LoRA-Mixer as a framework for validating the loss, and its abstract highlights superiority over routing-specific baselines with revised headline gains. The central claims of serial integration, architecture compatibility, modular reuse, and data-efficient routing remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds an information-bottleneck and optimization-curvature interpretation of RSL, an exploratory-routing explanation for the 4K performance dip, and a rationale for excluding STS-B. It also interprets the new generalization and resource results. The fixed-top-K and layer-redundancy limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds dataset split statistics, software versions, batching, loss weights, schedules, validation procedures, resource measurements, parameter accounting, and a code-access URL. V1 mainly supplied hardware, AdamW, learning rate, and adapter configuration. V2 omits the optimizer name and inconsistently gives lambda as 0.5 in A.6 and 0.05 in A.8.

R1.justification: V2 expands positioning toward specialized routing methods through PHATGOOSE, GMoE, DS-MoE, and AESL references and comparisons. Its bibliography also adds other LLM/vision works while dropping several original dataset and backbone references, including GSM8K, ARC, Mistral, and Falcon-Mamba sources. These changes extend beyond citation-style conversion.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, setup, loss explanation, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Existing theoretical material moves into the main text, several analyses move into the appendix, and appendices A–F plus the NeurIPS checklist are replaced by eighteen appendix subsections. Acknowledgments and a separate LLM-use statement are added.

P2.justification: V2 adds numerous tables displaying new comparisons, dataset statistics, resource measurements, hyperparameters, and architecture details. It relocates existing top-K and cross-domain displays, removes the individual-expert table, and changes the conference typography, headers, and page composition. Most existing diagrams and plotted analyses are reused.

improvement.justification: Controlled routing-loss comparisons and PHATGOOSE generalization tests strengthen evidence for the central routing claims, while resource measurements and implementation details address gaps acknowledged in v1. The net gain is limited by conflicting lambda settings, removal of the expert-ablation table behind a surviving 'Table ??' reference, and expanded theory that leaves the original entropy-sign inconsistency unresolved: minimizing the negative-entropy term rewards higher entropy, while the specialization explanation claims entropy suppression.
